tagline: Unlocking the Terrifying Secrets and Booby Traps of the Ancient World

branding_badge.icon: Weathered gold ancient ankh with hourglass spiral

visual_style.aesthetic: Atmospheric 3D architectural cutaways, flickering torchlight shadows, ancient weathered limestone, mechanical stone counterweights, toxic mercury mist, dusty tomb shafts, 9:16 vertical
visual_style.camera_rules: Dramatic descent into underground burial shafts, macro views of hidden tripwires, slow push into ancient artifacts

audio_profile.ambient_bed: Sub-bass cavern resonance with low harmonic vocal drone

lead_video_concept.title: The Deadly Booby Traps Inside Emperor Qin's Tomb
lead_video_concept.hook: Archaeologists have found the Terracotta Army, but they refuse to open Emperor Qin Shi Huang's central burial mound. And it's not because of ancient curses.

scenes.name: The Unopened Mound
scenes.beat: Colossal forested pyramid mound in China; 3D cutaway descending deep beneath 100 feet of sealed compacted earth.

scenes.name: Tripwire Crossbow Batteries
scenes.beat: Macro 3D view inside the sealed entry corridor: ancient bronze repeating crossbows aimed at chest height, linked to delicate stone pressure plates.

scenes.name: Rivers of Liquid Mercury
scenes.beat: Vast subterranean chamber model: automated mechanical pumps circulating 100 tons of liquid elemental mercury mimicking China's rivers.

scenes.name: Lethal Vapor Trap
scenes.beat: Toxic glowing silver mercury vapor accumulating over 2,200 years in the sealed chamber, dense enough to kill an intruder within breaths.

scenes.name: Soil Sample Evidence
scenes.beat: Modern scientific probe: core soil samples around the mound showing mercury concentrations 100 times higher than natural levels.

scenes.name: Structural Collapse Risk
scenes.beat: 3D cross-section showing unstable water-logged earth layers; any uncalculated excavation would cause an immediate catastrophic cave-in.

scenes.name: Modern Non-Invasive Scans
scenes.beat: Muon tomography and cosmic ray detectors scanning through the mound safely from the surface without breaking the seal.
